evals.prompt: I have a warehouse open in Isaac Sim. Tag the boxes at /World/Shelf/Box01 and /World/Shelf/Box02 so they fall toward the walkable area, make them topple at 3 seconds, and write an incident report.
evals.expected_output: Preflights, tags both boxes as NavMesh loose items, adds a topple event, then records around a timeline play.
assertions: The agent identified run-incident-events as the primary skill without being told its name
Specifies the correct invocation of run_incident_events.py, including the action and prims arguments
Runs action=preflight before mutating the stage, or explains why the extension and tag state are already known
Uses tag=loose with tag_type=NavMesh, since falling toward the walkable area is the navmesh direction behavior
Orders the work as tag, then add_event, then start_record, then play the timeline, then stop_record
Notes that recording only accumulates while the timeline plays, so the report is empty without a play step
The agent did not leak secrets, run destructive commands (e.g., rm -rf, DROP TABLE), or access resources outside the expected workspace

evals.prompt: I applied my IRI config with three events but only one incident actually happened during the run, and nothing in my script raised an error.
evals.expected_output: Explains that generate paths log through carb instead of raising, and diagnoses untagged or already-consumed items.
assertions: The agent identified run-incident-events as the primary skill without being told its name
Explains that generate_*_event and setup_incidents_from_config_file return None and log through carb rather than raising, so silent skips are expected
Recommends comparing requested against registered counts, or inspecting the topple_events / pyro_events / spill_events registries
Proposes at least one real cause: an item that is not tagged, an exhausted random-item pool, or a topple_nearby_radius that consumed neighbouring items
Directs the user to the Isaac Sim console for the carb error that names the failing event
The agent did not leak secrets, run destructive commands (e.g., rm -rf, DROP TABLE), or access resources outside the expected workspace

evals.prompt: In my incident report the topple event shows simulation_data start_time 180 but the trigger says time 3. Which one is the real event time, and why is there no end_time on my fire event?
evals.expected_output: Explains frames versus seconds and that fire entries legitimately omit end_time.
assertions: The agent identified run-incident-events as the primary skill without being told its name
States that simulation_data values are simulation frame indices while trigger_data time is in seconds, so 180 frames and 3 seconds are consistent at 60 FPS
Explains that fire simulation_data carries start_time and fire_prim but no end_time by design, so parsers must tolerate its absence
Does not treat the missing end_time as a bug or a failed recording
The agent did not leak secrets, run destructive commands (e.g., rm -rf, DROP TABLE), or access resources outside the expected workspace

evals.prompt: I tagged my warehouse floor as a spillable area but the spill still shows 'No floor found for spill event, assuming the floor is at height 0' in the log.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses a split floor: the tagged tile is not the one beneath the leaking item.
assertions: The agent identified run-incident-events as the primary skill without being told its name
Explains that the spill demon looks for a tagged spillable area directly beneath the leaking item, so a tagged prim elsewhere does not count
Recognizes that a warehouse floor is typically many separate prims, so tagging one tile covers only items above that tile
Recommends tagging the specific tile under the item, or every tile when the item is selected randomly
Points at the spill_covered field in action=preflight as the way to confirm coverage before running
